paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Comparison" presents a side-by-side comparison of accuracy percentages between two methods—Vanilla CoT (light yellow bars) and TLDR (Ours, green bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage (ranging from 0% to 100%, with major ticks every 20%), while the horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. The chart includes delta annotations above each pair of bars indicating the change in accuracy from Vanilla CoT to TLDR: -1.7% for GSM8K (Vanilla CoT: 89.4%, TLDR: 87.7%), +0.6% for MATH500 (Vanilla CoT: 86.8%, TLDR: 87.4%), -1.7% for AIME (Vanilla CoT: 42.9%, TLDR: 41.2%), and +1.6% for AMC (Vanilla CoT: 81.5%, TLDR: 83.1%). The bars are grouped by dataset, with each group containing two bars (Vanilla CoT and TLDR) side by side. The chart is sorted in an arbitrary order of datasets and does not emphasize any specific bar beyond the delta labels. The legend indicates that Vanilla CoT is represented by light yellow, and TLDR (Ours) by green. The visual presentation suggests that TLDR maintains or slightly improves accuracy over Vanilla CoT in most cases, particularly on MATH500 and AMC, while showing a small decrease on GSM8K and AIME.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Comparison" presents a side-by-side comparison of accuracy (%) between two methods—Vanilla CoT (light yellow bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark green bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 0 to 100 in increments of 20, with dashed horizontal gridlines. The horizontal axis lists the datasets in left-to-right order. For each dataset, two bars are shown: the Vanilla CoT bar is on the left, and the TLDR (Ours) bar is on the right. The chart includes numerical labels on top of each bar indicating the exact accuracy percentage and a delta value (in red or green) showing the change relative to Vanilla CoT. On GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 89.4% accuracy, while TLDR achieves 87.7% (a -1.7% change). On MATH500, Vanilla CoT scores 86.8%, and TLDR scores 87.4% (+0.6%). On AIME, Vanilla CoT scores 42.9%, and TLDR scores 41.2% (-1.7%). On AMC, Vanilla CoT scores 81.5%, and TLDR scores 83.1% (+1.6%). The bars are arranged in groups per dataset, with no stacking or overlapping, and the chart does not visually emphasize any particular bar through shading or outlines. The legend at the top right identifies the two methods by color. The overall trend indicates that TLDR maintains or slightly improves accuracy compared to Vanilla CoT across the four datasets, with the exception of GSM8K and AIME, where accuracy slightly decreases.
